correctness.rationale: For p>=1, q>=2, edge gradients are independent coordinates of the polar cube. A returning two-edge arm has squared uncentered contribution 1 rather than 5; choosing the better straight-arm sign increases centered squared norm by at least 4-8/N>0 since N=1+p+2q>=6. Thus only fully straight long arms maximize. Direct imbalance of 3 sum(long signs)+sum(short signs) gives d=0,1 or exceptional 2. Opposite polar facet normals force global radius from the origin. The contact-binomial sum and the groupwise sign zero-sum representation yield the stated rank and p=3 parity dimension. Own exact exhaustive signed-gradient checks for arm vectors (1,2,2), (1,2,2,2), (1,1,1,2,2) and exact rank checks for p=3,q=2..5 match all stated norms/contacts/dimensions; these are finite corroboration, not an all-p,q proof.
